description: Clique structure decoded from page 30 diagram (overlapping circles) and user corrections. Cliques overlap — girls appear in multiple groups.
data_source: User corrections to diagram + consultant interview notes

cliques.notes: CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Ada describes two overlapping triads, not a single five-person group. This triad formed organically when Ada and Mia started saying hi to Lou after she drifted from the Indian girls. Lou was previously best friends with Alicia. She now runs intel-gathering operations — proximity tests, mood reads — for Ada's group. Ada values Lou instrumentally: 'she's useful to have.' UPDATE: Lou still partly friends with Alicia but reports that Alicia and Anyeshka 'are starting to be rude to her.'

CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Second of Ada's two overlapping triads. Originally was Mia/Natalia/Olivia N/Alicia; Ada joined, Alicia separated. Now Ada/Mia/Natalia. Olivia N is peripheral (sits across from them at lunch, hangs out with Kiara at recess). The analytical label 'Core Five' merged these two triads plus Olivia N; Ada does not perceive it that way.
Mia bridges into this group. Olivia Q (Bareres), Milan, and Ellie (Gryser) are the 'random Chinese girls' Ashley references as her #1. This group does not tend to interact with the Indian girls.

CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Three-pack only. Alice is a separate pairing (see alice_alicia). Cross-group friendship spanning Bell and Babu homerooms. Alicia proactively befriends newcomers/isolates — when Lou first arrived, Alicia walked over and said 'Sup, Lou?'

CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Not all members from Babu's class — group is cross-homeroom. Anjolie and Lyla are NOT really in this group (previous report overstated). Lou is 'still kind of in the group, she just doesn't hang out with anyone that much' — peripheral, not departed. Lyla 'might be joining' but this is tentative. Maperi (Turkish) is embedded. This group does not tend to interact with the Chinese girls.

Madeline and Sanvi were friends; Alicia recently joined after her falling out with Mia and Ada. Madeline now acts as Alicia's proxy/enforcer — she confronts Ada's group on Alicia's behalf (Steam Day incident: accused them of glaring, stealing friends, told them to 'leave us alone'). Alicia stays back while Madeline does the confrontation.

Pairing from far-right circle on diagram. Subunit within the broader Indian girls group. Per Ada, Kaisha is the ecosystem's neutral mediator — collects info from both sides of conflicts and relays it without taking sides. Ada also uses her as a social shield (Steam Day). Kaisha's mediation reportedly fails with Alicia because 'Alicia usually doesn't understand.'

Self-contained Bell homeroom trio. CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Lyla was never friends with Alice ('they were actually enemies') and never friends with Anjolie. Previous claims about Alice-Lyla breakup and Lyla-Anjolie friendship are contradicted. Lyla (L-I-L-A) and Leela (L-E-E-L-A, Clendenon) are two separate people.

CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Alice befriended Alicia about a week BEFORE the split with Lyla. Alice is still friends with Alicia. Earlier claims about Alice-Lyla friendship are contradicted by Ada's latest account (see Lyla discrepancy). Ada notes: 'I don't know if Alicia knows that I see Alice as a friend, but her and Alice probably know that they're friends.'

disputes.allegation: Alicia alleges Mia and Ada are stealing friends and telling secrets.
disputes.ada_side: Ada says things were 'kind of nice' with Alicia initially, but: (1) Alicia didn't share snacks, (2) in music class Alicia would always grab Natalia as her partner because she sat closest — Ada and Mia always worked together but wanted to work with Natalia too, (3) Alicia 'doesn't really like [Ada/Mia] too much', (4) Alicia 'got a little bossy' and 'started to become the leader of our group.' Then as weeks went on Alicia 'started to kind of separate from our group' — and that's how the Ada/Mia/Natalia trio formed.
disputes.context: Alicia was originally part of the Mia/Natalia/Olivia group. She is still friends with Natalia and Olivia but not Mia or Ada. Per Ada, the separation was gradual — Alicia pulled away after becoming bossy, rather than being expelled. Natalia is the contested resource — both sides want her as a partner/friend, and physical proximity in music class gave Alicia first-mover advantage.

disputes.notes: Madeline H and Ada were best friends. Per Ada, the breakup was 'kind of similar to Alicia' — Madeline got oversensitive, mad about little things, and bossy. Specifics: (1) Madeline put notes in Ada's mailbox threatening to end the friendship if Ada didn't do certain things, (2) they wasted recesses having repeated talks about the same issues, (3) Madeline got mad when others didn't play with her — e.g., Alice went to play football and Madeline complained 'it's no fair, why is Alice not playing with me?', (4) when Ada tried to explain it was fine, Madeline said 'I bet you don't know how to survive in the wild' and walked away angrily, (5) Madeline got bossy at playdates, pulling Ada away from activities, (6) pool incident — Madeline counted down from 10 ordering Ada and Arlo (sibling?) to get out of the pool. Ada decided in fourth grade that Madeline 'is not the friend for me' but hasn't told her yet: 'I really don't want to see her face when I tell her this.' Note: the 'Alice' in this story is a DIFFERENT Alice from third grade who has since moved schools — NOT Alice from Bell homeroom who broke up with Lyla.
disputes.ada_pattern: Ada describes both Alicia and Madeline with nearly identical complaints: bossiness, controlling behavior, getting mad over little things. Ada's response in both cases is gradual disengagement rather than confrontation.

disputes.notes: DISCREPANCY. Ada debrief (earlier): Alice and Lyla were best friends who 'broke up' — detailed accounts from both sides. Ada's report review (current): 'Lyla was never friends with Alice. They were actually enemies.' And 'Lyla was never friends with Anjolie either.' These accounts cannot both be true. Alice befriended Alicia about a week before the Lyla split. Lyla interview needed to resolve.

disputes.allegation: Lou felt the Indian girls 'discluded' her (Ada's word). Not outright meanness — more gradual exclusion.
disputes.context: CORRECTION (Ada's report review): Lou is 'still kind of in the group, she just doesn't hang out with anyone that much.' The migration is partial, not complete — Lou is peripheral to both the Indian girls and Ada's group. Lou also reports Alicia and Anyeshka 'are starting to be rude to her,' further complicating her position.

disputes.name: Head-top confrontation (precedes Steam Day recess)
sequence: Ada and Mia tell Alicia: 'Don't call us by our nicknames anymore, you're not our friend.'
Alicia: 'Fine, I'm fine with that.'
Alicia then head-tops them ('for the ten billionth time even though we asked her not to').
Alicia claims they never told her to stop.
Mia head-tops Alicia back and runs away.
Ada attempts to head-top Alicia; Alicia blocks Ada's hand and hits Ada's head.
Alicia accuses Ada of hitting her head; Ada says she didn't touch it.
disputes.context: Head-top is a game where you tap someone's head to give them the 'head top.' You can block by placing your hand on your head. The game is social currency — doing it to someone who told you to stop is a provocation. This incident directly preceded the Steam Day recess fight.

disputes.name: Madeline-Alicia alliance forming
evidence: During Steam Day recess, Alicia was walking alone; Madeline came over to her.
Madeline asked Ada's group why they were 'talking behind Alicia's back.'
Madeline said 'Can you stay away, we are going to have a private talk' and had private talk with Alicia.
After the fight, Ada saw Madeline on monkey bars with Anyeshka and Navya — 'I knew something was up.'
Ada: 'They might have more allies and friends, but at least we have more brains.'
disputes.ada_theory: Madeline may have come over because she either (1) saw the fight firsthand (Johnson's class may have come out to recess first) — 'me tapping Alicia's head, me yelling at Alicia, me arguing,' or (2) saw Alicia looking sad and went to check on her, and Alicia spilled what happened.
disputes.analytical_note: Madeline with Anyeshka and Navya on the monkey bars is a cross-group signal — Madeline (Johnson) linking up with Indian girls (Babu). Maperi was also there but 'just swinging on the monkey bars and having fun' — not part of the alliance.

disputes.name: Direct confrontation with Alicia (3/25)
sequence: Extra recess after PE. Alicia is with Alice.
Ada and Mia approach to tell Alicia to quit talking behind their back.
Alicia: 'No, I'm having a private talk.'
Alicia and Alice go have their private talk (about Ada/Mia — 'Duh!').
Alicia returns: 'What do you want?'
Ada/Mia: 'Can you stop talking behind our back?'
Alicia goes into 'full yelling mode': 'I can express my feelings with my friends!'
Ada/Mia: 'Yeah, but can you just not talk about us behind our back?'
Alicia: 'Well, why can't I express my feelings with my friends?' and 'Why do you guys talk behind my back?'
Alicia starts walking away.
Ada yells back: 'Well, why do you talk behind ours?' and 'We're just expressing our feelings!'
disputes.context: FIRST direct confrontation in the data. Ada has previously avoided face-to-face conflict (proxy relay, quiet disengagement). Here she initiates direct engagement. Alicia's defense is rights-based: 'I can express my feelings.' Ada throws Alicia's exact language back at her. Alice is present throughout as Alicia's companion, reinforcing the Alice-Alicia pairing.

disputes.name: Madeline gossips to Devon (3/25)
disputes.content: Madeline told Devon at recess: 'Ada bullies me and she also talks behind my back and glares at me.'
disputes.analytical_note: Madeline's narrative campaign has expanded beyond Alicia's inner circle to Devon, a Johnson classmate whose top friends (Olivia N, Julia — both Bell) are outside the conflict. But the intelligence backfired — Devon reported it to Ada. Devon is either neutral or Ada-leaning. This is the first confirmed instance of Madeline's gossip reaching Ada through an unintended channel.

disputes.name: Anyeshka bathroom confession (3/25)
sequence: In the bathroom, Ada asks Anyeshka: 'Does Alicia talk about me?'
Anyeshka: 'Why should I tell you?'
Ada: 'Please, I won't tell anyone!'
Anyeshka: 'Fine, but you have to promise because then Alicia will get really mad at me.'
Anyeshka reveals: Alicia 'always says that you are stealing her friends and making her feel discluded even though you guys are not friends.'
Ada asks how often. Anyeshka: 'Every two recesses.'
disputes.analytical_note: Ada has turned one of Alicia's core three-pack allies into an intelligence source. Anyeshka's fear ('Alicia will get really mad at me') shows she knows she's betraying a confidence. Ada promised not to tell — but she told us. The content confirms Alicia's complaints are regular ('every two recesses') and consistent ('stealing friends, making her feel discluded'). This is Ada's most successful intelligence coup: direct from inside Alicia's inner circle.

disputes.name: Alice spreads narrative to Lyla (3/25)
sequence: Alice was with Alicia 'to talk with her about stuff and also she helped spread it to Lyla.'
Before Alice could finish talking with Lyla, Ada and Mia approached: 'Alice, are you talking about us?'
Alice: 'No.'
Ada to Lyla: 'Seriously, what did she tell you?'
Lyla: 'Why are you guys stealing Alicia's friends?'
disputes.analytical_note: Alice's role expands from companion (Group H) to active propagandist — she's spreading Alicia's 'stealing friends' narrative to the Annie/Julia/Lyla trio (Group G). Lyla's parroting of the accusation confirms the message was received. This connects Alicia's lunch group (Annie/Julia/Lyla) to the broader narrative campaign. The information chain: Alicia → Alice → Lyla. Ada caught it mid-transfer.

Former best friend of Alicia, now in Ada's triad (Ada/Mia/Lou). Still peripheral to Indian girls group. Runs recon operations (proximity tests, mood reads) on Alicia. Valued instrumentally by Ada for insider knowledge. Reports Alicia and Anyeshka are 'being rude to her' — the Lou-Alicia bond is fraying.

ethnic_dynamics.chinese_indian_separation: Chinese girls and Indian girls don't tend to interact. Mia and Ada are exceptions.
ethnic_dynamics.chinese_group: Confirmed members: Ashley, Mia, Olivia Q, Milan, Ellie. Centered in Johnson homeroom but spans Bareres and Gryser.
ethnic_dynamics.indian_group: CORRECTION: Confirmed core: Navya, Anyeshka, Kaisha. Group is cross-homeroom (not all Babu). Anjolie and Lyla are NOT really in it. Lou is still peripheral ('kind of in the group'). Maperi (Turkish) is embedded. Not purely ethnic.

lunchtime_seating.arrangement: Each class has its own table. Tables are assigned by homeroom.
lunchtime_seating.table_order_note: Bell is between Babu and Johnson. After Johnson: Bareres, then Clendenon, then Gryser. Ada was uncertain about exact order beyond Johnson.
lunchtime_seating.bell_table_detail: Ada, Mia, Natalia sit on the same bench. Olivia N sits across from them. Alice might join. Mostly it's Ada/Mia/Natalia/Olivia.
lunchtime_seating.johnson_table_detail: Madeline sits somewhere near Jane, Margaret, and Abby.

snack_sharing_methods.source: Ada remarks (latest). Describes how Ada and Mia share snacks covertly in Bell's classroom.
methods: 1. Wait for designated snack time (Ms. Bell lets them 'chillax and eat snack for three minutes'). Ada walks to Mia's desk.
2. When working in partners — choose each other, bring snacks over.
3. At the carpet — sneakily share snacks with each other.
4. 'Throwing away stuff method' — Ada rips off a piece of trash, goes to throw it in the trash can, gives Mia snack on the way there, receives 'payment' on the way back.
snack_sharing_methods.analytical_note: The elaborate covert methods suggest snack-sharing is both a bonding ritual and a minor form of rule-breaking that reinforces the Ada-Mia pair bond. The 'payment' framing is notable — a miniature economy of reciprocity.

steam_day_explained.format: Rotating stations. Some stations pair two classes together. After stations: either stay with own class, or whole 4th+5th grade in cafeteria for experiment, or in classroom with parents. Different people at different times.
steam_day_explained.examples: Art = drawing, Science = elephant toothpaste, Technology = snap circuits

popularity_hierarchy.notes: #3 most popular boy. Two other boys' names listed alongside him but illegible.

crush_subplot.description: Barack is suspected of having a crush on Jane. Natalia told Jane she saw Barack reading Babysitter's Club (implying he's trying to impress her or share her interests). The girls debate whether it's better for Jane that the weird boys (Barack, Sid) have a crush on her than nobody at all.

ada_mom.position: Wants to intervene. Proposed Ada broker a truce by bringing snacks to girls she's fighting with. Concerned conflict is 'getting out of hand' and girls are 'fighting for no reason.' Goal: civility, not necessarily friendship.
ada_mom.relationship_to_madeline_family: Ada's mom used to be friends with Madeline's mom. Stopped talking to her about a year ago because Madeline's mom would always ask for free babysitting and be late to pick up her three girls (Madeline is the eldest). This means the Ada-Madeline parental friendship predates and mirrors the girls' breakup — both relationships ended with one party feeling exploited by the other.
ada_mom.relationship_to_mia_family: Mia lives on the same street as Ada. Their moms are friends. This means the Ada-Mia pair bond has a parental infrastructure: the mothers' friendship likely facilitates playdates, proximity, and shared social context.

ada_dad.position: Thinks the situation will sort itself out. Adults shouldn't insert themselves.

ada.position: Doesn't like the idea of emailing the school counselor.

analytical_notes: The parent-level relationships mirror the girls' social structure. Ada's mom cut off Madeline's mom for being exploitative (demanding babysitting, being late) — the same pattern Ada describes in Madeline: bossiness, controlling, demanding. Whether Ada learned this framing from her mother or arrived at it independently, the parallel is striking.

Mia living on Ada's street explains the depth and durability of the Ada-Mia pair bond. Geographic proximity + parental friendship = the strongest possible foundation for a childhood friendship. This is why Ada-Mia is the load-bearing axis of Bloc 1 — it has structural support that purely school-based friendships lack.
Madeline has two younger sisters. Being the eldest of three may inform her caretaking/managing behavior that Ada and others describe as 'bossy.'

The snack-truce proposal was assessed as likely counterproductive: in Ada's social economy, snack-sharing is a membership ritual and gatekeeping criterion ('Alicia could have joined if she shared snacks'). Offering snacks to Alicia would read as a power move, not an olive branch.
Counselor email was assessed as risky due to Ada's confidentiality constraint — if the counselor investigates and Ada is identified as the source, it could damage her social position.
